subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw support per-agent managed plugin installs now, and if so what is the durable contract for record identity, discovery/activation scope, update/uninstall behavior, and plugin trust boundaries?
rationale: The PR adds public CLI and persisted install-record surface in a security-sensitive plugin execution path, and automation cannot safely choose the permanent scoped identity and activation semantics.

options.title: Define the scoped install contract first
options.body: Pause merge until maintainers decide record identity, activation/discovery scope, update/uninstall cleanup, validation, docs, and security policy, then repair this branch to match it.

options.title: Narrow this PR to non-user-facing groundwork
options.body: Remove the public `--agent` flag and keep only internal refactoring or tests that do not create scoped persisted state yet.

options.title: Close in favor of the canonical issue
options.body: Leave https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97749 as the product-design tracker and ask for a fresh implementation after the contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Define the scoped install contract first
recommendation.body: Pause merge until maintainers decide record identity, activation/discovery scope, update/uninstall cleanup, validation, docs, and security policy, then repair this branch to match it.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans plugin control-plane architecture, public CLI/config contract, and security-sensitive ownership boundaries where history and CODEOWNERS context point most strongly to this owner.
